plūrĭfārĭam , adv. id.,
I.in many parts or places (post-Aug.), Suet. Aug. 46; 80; id. Tib. 43; id. Calig. 54; id. Ner. 24; id. Vit. 9: “gladiatoria munera plurifariam exhibuit,” id. Claud. 21 (al. plurifaria).—
II. In many ways, manifoldly, variously (post-class.), App. Flor. p. 357, 37; “p. 178 Bip.: mons Taurus pro gentium ac linguarum varietate plurifariam nominatus,” Sol. 38 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
